title: Principal Enterprise Architect
descriptionHtml:
Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Role:

We are looking for a curious, smart, and “learn it all” Architect with proven experience and a passion for designing transformative solution architectures for our prospects and customers. This high-impact role demands a unique blend of deep technical expertise and executive presence, requiring you to confidently present to C-level executives and translate their strategic goals into actionable technical plans. You will work with technical teams at our prospects and customers to design architectures that drive enterprise modernization, leveraging techniques like capability mapping and exploring innovative solutions with Agentic AI.

Your primary goal is to support our growing sales team in achieving revenue goals by unlocking technical blockers and partnering closely with our Sales, Value Engineering, Product Management, Data Ops, and Information Security teams. You will be responsible for supporting engagements with new prospects as well as existing customers that look to expand their footprint. Measures of success include new customer acquisition rates, retention, up-selling, and contribution to overall sales team and business success.

The work you’ll do:

  • Lead and define the overall architecture, data, and cloud strategy for our largest client accounts, leveraging expertise like enterprise modernization and capability mapping.
  • Confidently engage with and present to customer C-level executives, aligning their strategic objectives with the Celonis technical strategy.
  • Drive innovation by identifying and architecting solutions that leverage emergent technologies, including Agentic AI.
  • Be the bridge between our product & engineering teams within Celonis and the client's teams to provide the best technical services.
  • Assess the IT landscape maturity of our customer installed base for the region.
  • Participate in pre-Sales and post-Sales phases by engaging with customer Architecture and security teams.
  • Coach and guide Celonis consulting teams and ecosystem partners on technical implementation issues such as architecture, integration, performance, and scalability.
  • Develop re-usable assets for the consulting teams on projects.
  • Develop customer-facing position papers, assets, and thought leadership presentations on architecture and innovation with Celonis.
  • Create technical designs and presentations for internal and client stakeholders.

The qualifications you need:

  • 10 to 15 years of relevant experience (e.g., Software vendor Architect, CTO at a top consulting firm, or Enterprise Architect at a customer).
  • Proven ability to think strategically, connecting technical solutions to business value and customer objectives.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a proven track record of presenting complex technical concepts and strategic visions to C-level executives.
  • Demonstrated experience in Capability Mapping, Enterprise Modernization, and a strong understanding of Agentic AI
  • Strong understanding of cloud-native architectures, SaaS solutions, ERP (particularly SAP),  Salesforce, Dynamics CRM or ServiceNow), cybersecurity posture fundamentals, API ecosystems, along with legacy on-premise enterprise architectures.
  • Strong background in Data Architecture, Integrations patterns, and a development background in data-related languages (SQL, Python, etc.)
  • Strong technical background with a focus on system integrations, data operations, and automation capabilities.
  • The ability to comfortably switch from explaining an architecture diagram to an environment where you have coded or assembled a demo of that architecture.
  • MSc degree in Computer Science or an equivalent in an Information Technology-related field.
  • Fluency in English is required; an additional language such as Spanish, German, French or Italian is a strong advantage.

Additional qualifications preferred:

  • Celonis Certifications and Experience with OCPM and Case Centric Data Pipelines.
  • AWS/Azure/GCP Certifications.
  • ESB / ETL Certifications (Mulesoft, Oracle, SAP, Talend, Informatica).
  • TOGAF/Zachmann Certification.
  • Experience in at least two domains among: Finance, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer/Consumer Management (Service, Order Management, Sales), HR, Procurement.
  • Experience in at least two industries among: Consumer Goods, Banking, Pharma, Aerospace, Telco, Transport.

What Celonis can offer you:

  • Pioneer Innovation: Work with the global leader in Process Mining and the Process Intelligence Graph to shape the future of AI-driven business operations.
  • Ownership from Day 1: Every full-time "Celonaut" is an owner, receiving Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and merit-based refresh grants.
  • Unrivaled Family Support: Benefit from our inclusive parental leave policy—24 weeks of fully paid leave for primary carers and 12 weeks for supporting carers, available from your first day of employment.
  • Work-Life Integration: Enjoy Unlimited PTO (in applicable regions) and generous PTO globally, as well as a flexible hybrid work model that balances remote focus with vibrant office collaboration.
  • Continuous Growth: Elevate your skills through our 70-20-10 learning framework, mentorship programs, and access to a dedicated learning platform.
  • Holistic Well-being: Prioritize your health with subsidized Wellhub memberships, mental health counseling, and dedicated "Wellness Weeks" that prioritize work/life balance.
  • Drive Sustainability: Participate in annual Impact Days, where you receive paid time off to volunteer for community and environmental causes with your local office, or virtually.
  • Global Inclusion & Belonging: Find community through our Inclusion Think Tank and participate in our annual Inclusion Days, ensuring every voice is heard and valued.
  • Value-Driven Impact: Join a mission-led organization where our core values—Live for Customer Value, The Best Team Wins, We Own It, and Earth Is Our Future—drive every decision.

About Us:

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI, empowering organizations to analyze, design, and operate AI-driven processes. The Celonis Platform is powered by the Celonis Context Model, which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence to create a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can understand — turning AI’s operational blind spots into operational clarity. Industry-leading companies around the world trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. Celonis is headquartered in Munich, Germany, and New York City, USA, with more than 20 offices worldwide.

Get familiar with the Celonis Process Intelligence Platform by watching this video.

Celonis Inclusion Statement:

At Celonis, we believe our people make us who we are and that “The Best Team Wins”. We know that the best teams are made up of people who bring different perspectives to the table. And when everyone feels included, able to speak up and knows their voice is heard - that's when creativity and innovation happen.

Your Privacy:

Any information you submit to Celonis as part of your application will be processed in accordance with Celonis’ Accessibility and Candidate Notices

By submitting this application, you confirm that you agree to the storing and processing of your personal data by Celonis as described in our Privacy Notice for the Application and Hiring Process.

Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools

We rely on an artificial intelligence tool to match the information from your resume to the relevant Celonis job descriptions. This processing is limited to the information provided in your resume or in your candidate profile. The tool produces a match score per candidate for a role, suggests preliminary ranking, and provides recommendations.

The tool is only used for support in parts of the job application process, including to facilitate the identification of the relevant Celonis Jobs for candidates and recruiters. All final decisions are made by hiring managers and the Celonis talent acquisition team. title: Principal of backend
descriptionHtml:
About SchemeServe

SchemeServe is insurance software like no other.

Hosted in the cloud for MGAs, brokers and insurers, the SchemeServe platform boasts unique flexibility, unstoppable innovation and truly Obsessive Support.

Started in 2000 by our CEO, Adam, SchemeServe has grown from strength to strength, never having taken outside investment. We're proud of how far we've come and how loyal we've stayed to our Core Values.

We're fully remote (we were doing it before it was fashionable!), although we get together twice a year for Team Retreats.

We prize self-development and encourage everyone to keep learning and challenging themselves. Free books? Mentoring? Professional development? You got it.

We also offer flexible working, paid charity days, a fantastic, relaxed and open company culture and free biscuits through the post.

We genuinely believe this is the best place you could ever work.

If you're excited, good! So are we.

Come and join the Insurtech revolution!

Principal Backend Engineer

UK Remote

We're looking for an exceptional Principal Backend Engineer to help make backend engineering across SchemeServe better.

You'll be one of the most technically experienced engineers in the organisation and the CTO's primary technical partner for backend engineering, helping shape our architecture, engineering principles and technical direction.

But this isn't primarily a feature delivery role and your job isn't to personally build everything you help design.

Your real job is to make our engineering organisation better at building great software.

You'll work alongside engineers and teams, helping solve difficult problems, challenging their thinking and developing their technical skills and judgement.

What We Mean By Principal



This is a deeply technical role.

You'll need the depth to understand complex backend systems, architecture, security, performance, resilience and maintainability; review designs and implementations; spot risks; and challenge experienced engineers.

But technical knowledge alone isn't enough.

We want someone who understands there isn't always one "correct" way to build software.

Patterns, standards and best practices are useful tools. They aren't commandments.

We care about finding the most appropriate solution to the problem in front of us.

That means understanding the problem, business, existing platform, risks and likely future – and making pragmatic decisions based on the trade-offs.

Sometimes the right answer will be a new service or technology.

Sometimes it'll be improving what we already have.

Sometimes the boring solution really is the best solution.

We're quite comfortable with that.

How You'll Lead



Success in this role comes through influence rather than authority.

We don't want every difficult technical decision to end with:

"We'd better ask the Principal Engineer."

If an engineer proposes an approach you disagree with, we don't just want you to replace it with your own.

Understand their thinking. Ask questions. Challenge assumptions. Explore the trade-offs. Share your experience.

And be prepared to change your own mind too.

The goal is to leave that engineer better equipped to solve the next problem, not just holding the answer to this one.

Your technical impact should multiply through the people around you.

You'll remain close enough to the code to understand what's actually happening and occasionally roll up your sleeves to prototype, investigate a difficult problem or unblock a team.

But if after a year you've personally written loads of brilliant software while everyone around you is working exactly as they were before, we haven't succeeded.

The Technical Challenge



Our platform has been evolving for more than 25 years.

At its heart is a mature C# .NET Framework 4.7 monolith, alongside an expanding ecosystem of modern C# .NET 10 and TypeScript services.

Our backend estate includes:


  • .NET Framework and modern C#/.NET.
  • TypeScript services.
  • Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Redis.
  • Azure cloud infrastructure.
  • Cloudflare platform services.
  • API-first architecture.
  • Git-based development workflows.


We're continuing to modernise, but we're not interested in modernisation for modernisation's sake.

We aren't trying to win an award for having the most fashionable architecture diagram.

We want a secure, reliable and maintainable platform that can support SchemeServe for many years to come – and we want you to help us decide what should evolve and, just as importantly, what doesn't need changing.

What You'll Do



You'll work closely with our CTO and engineering teams to:


  • Shape our backend engineering strategy, architecture and technical direction.
  • Help engineers make better technical and architectural decisions.
  • Develop sensible engineering principles and guardrails without replacing good judgement with rules.
  • Guide the continued evolution of our monolith and modern service-based platform.
  • Coach and mentor engineers, developing their technical skills and judgement.
  • Review significant designs and architectural decisions and challenge unnecessary complexity.
  • Champion security, quality, testing, observability, resilience and performance.
  • Identify technical risks and help teams navigate them.
  • Evaluate technologies and patterns based on their value to SchemeServe rather than their popularity elsewhere.
  • Balance long-term engineering quality with short-term business needs.
  • Occasionally contribute directly to implementation when that's genuinely the best way to help.
  • Be a generally awesome person.


What We're Looking For



You'll need:


  • Deep expertise in modern backend engineering and strong commercial C#/.NET experience.
  • Strong knowledge of software architecture, distributed systems and API design.
  • Experience with mature legacy applications and modern service-oriented architectures.
  • Strong cloud architecture experience, ideally Azure.
  • Excellent understanding of databases, security, testing, maintainability and modern software delivery.
  • Experience shaping engineering principles and practices across teams.
  • A track record of making engineers around you better through mentoring, coaching and technical leadership.
  • The ability to challenge experienced engineers constructively without becoming a gatekeeper.
  • Strong opinions, loosely held – the confidence to challenge and the humility to change your mind.
  • Excellent communication and the ability to influence without relying on authority.
  • Excellent technical judgement, balancing quality, complexity, risk, cost and business value.


Most importantly, we're looking for someone who asks:

"What's the right solution for us?"

rather than:

"What's the way everyone else is doing it?"

Nice To Have


  • Experience modernising large monolithic applications.
  • Commercial TypeScript backend experience.
  • Cloudflare or edge technology experience.
  • SaaS platforms at scale.
  • Financial services, insurance or another regulated industry.
  • Observability, platform engineering or SRE experience.
  • AI-assisted development and engineering productivity tooling.


You don't need to tick every box.

If you've got the technical depth, judgement and ability to make engineers around you better, we'd rather have a conversation than lose a great candidate because you haven't used one particular technology.

What Success Looks Like



Within your first year:


  • Engineers are making stronger technical and architectural decisions with greater confidence.
  • Our engineering principles are understood rather than blindly followed.
  • Technical discussions are constructive, pragmatic and result in clear decisions.
  • Security, reliability, maintainability and performance concerns are identified earlier.
  • We've made sensible progress modernising our platform without adding complexity for complexity's sake.
  • You've made a lasting positive impact on both our software and the people who build it.


Ultimately, we don't want SchemeServe to become dependent on you for every difficult technical decision.

We want SchemeServe to become better at making those decisions because you're here.

Why Join SchemeServe?

  • Twice-yearly company retreats.
  • Flexible working.
  • Dedicated professional development support.
  • Paid charity days.

We are looking for a Principal Architect to define and drive the architectural vision of the software stack for the Graphcore ML accelerator.

In this role, you will shape the architecture of our software ecosystem and maintain a deep understanding of the product’s hardware and software components, their interfaces, and how they interact.

You are an excellent communicator, and you proactively convey the software architecture.

You bring a pragmatic, trade-off-aware approach to decision-making, fully recognising the impact of architectural choices on product direction and engineering outcomes.

The software architecture team is responsible for defining, maintaining and communicating the overarching architecture of our software stack, from firmware to ML frameworks.

The team works within the wider software organisation, partnering closely with engineering teams who deliver against this architectural vision. 

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Define & document the software architecture of the software stack.  
  • Work across different software domains to ensure a coherent end too end architecture.
  • Clearly communicate the software architecture to engineering teams.

  • Stay informed about trends and developments in the ML/software ecosystem.

  • Prototyping and validating architectural concepts through proof-of-concept implementations. 
  • Contribute to future and/or related product definitions with a forward-looking mindset, understanding and communicating the impact of future direction on software architecture. 
  • Work with the HW and Silicon architects to ensure product the needs of software stack. 
  • Ensure the software architecture meets the product requirements.  
  • Work closely with engineering, product, leadership, and partners to ensure alignment between business goals and architectural direction. 

Candidate Profile

Essential:

  • Expertise in one or more of these technologies; Firmware, Drivers, ML frameworks (PyTorch, Triton, etc), Collectives, HPC, Tooling, C & C++, CPU architectures.
  • Technical expertise in the ML accelerator software space.
  • Excellent communication skill, both written and verbal. 
  • Collaborative mindset and ability to influence. 
  • Pragmatic approach to decision making, being very aware of trade-offs and implications. 

Desirable

title: Proctor Quality and Learning Manager, Scaling Operations
descriptionHtml:
Our mission at Duolingo is to develop the best education in the world and make it universally available. It’s a big mission, and that’s where you come in!

At Duolingo, you’ll join a team that cares about educating our users, experimenting with big ideas, making fact-based decisions, and finding innovative solutions to complex problems. You’ll have limitless learning opportunities and daily collaborations with world-class minds — while doing work that’s both meaningful and fun.

Join our life-changing mission to develop education for our half a billion (and growing!) learners around the world. 

Read our blog to learn more.

About the role...

The Duolingo English Test (DET) is a high-stakes assessment used by institutions around the world. Its integrity depends on proctors making accurate, consistent, and defensible decisions — even when sessions present ambiguous evidence or new forms of cheating. As the Proctor Quality and Learning Manager (L3) in Scaling Operations, you will own the end-to-end quality standard and learning system that keep our global proctor network aligned and effective as security threats, technology, and workflows evolve. You’ll define what “correct” looks like, run our calibration and adjudication program, and build ongoing training that measurably improves decision quality. You will partner with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering to ensure our human and AI-assisted workflows meet rigorous accuracy standards before and after deployment. This is an individual-contributor role within DET Proctoring Operations, with functional leadership over Training Specialists and adjudicators executing the program.

🧠  You will...

  • Own the DET proctoring quality standard — maintain rubrics, decision rules, examples, and guidance that define accurate decisions across routine and difficult edge cases.
  • Lead calibration and adjudication — operate recurring Proctor Certification Test cycles, resolve disputed decisions, identify patterns of disagreement, and ensure outcomes are consistent and auditable.
  • Build and run an ongoing learning program — publish a forward-looking training calendar, deliver monthly interventions, and launch targeted training in response to quality signals, threats, or workflow changes.
  • Measure effectiveness — use calibration results, audits, and performance trends to identify learning needs, evaluate training impact, and decide when to clarify standards, retrain, or update guidance.
  • Guide specialist execution — set expectations for Training Specialists and adjudicators, assign deliverables, review outputs, and operate onboarding and certification that ramp new specialists quickly.
  • Maintain durable sources of truth — keep calibration, adjudication, and training runbooks current so critical processes are documented and auditable.
  • Evolve quality alongside proctoring — translate new threats and workflow changes into clear standards, training, and quality controls in partnership with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering.
  • Represent the proctoring craft — bring frontline proctor evidence into product experiments and workflow decisions; assess whether launched changes preserve decision quality.
  • Connect human and technology-assisted quality — establish benchmarks for AI-assisted workflows and validate automated capabilities against real sessions before deployment.

✅  You have...

  • 5+ years in assessment development, scoring/rater quality, certification, quality assurance, or a field involving complex, consequential judgments; experience aligning reviewers to a shared standard through calibration programs.
  • Adult-learning program experience spanning onboarding, certification, ongoing training, remediation, and effectiveness measurement (beyond one-off materials).
  • Exceptional attention to detail and strong judgment in ambiguous cases; ability to produce clear, defensible decisions and guidance.
  • Analytical fluency to interpret quality data, disagreement patterns, and performance trends and translate them into practical interventions.
  • Clear written and verbal communication; ability to turn complex standards into precise, usable guidance and explain difficult calls.
  • Cross-functional leadership without formal authority; experience directing contractors or partners toward clear accountability and outcomes.
  • Demonstrated skill in quality standards and rubric design, building living systems with decision logs, change histories, and controls for auditability.
  • Experience defining quality benchmarks and validation methods for human–technology workflows, including AI-assisted processes.
  • Adaptability — comfort revising standards and programs as risks, products, and technology change.

⭐  Exceptional candidates will have...

  • Experience in language assessment, test security, remote proctoring, trust and safety, or fraud prevention in high-integrity environments.
  • Experience maintaining quality across large, distributed examiner/rater/reviewer/contractor populations.
  • Familiarity with assessment concepts such as inter-rater agreement, reliability, standardization, and performance monitoring.
  • Experience designing quality systems that span human judgment and technology-assisted workflows.
  • Familiarity with learning-management systems, assessment platforms, quality-audit tools, or operational analytics.

The offered salary is dependent upon several factors, including work experience, skills, and internal peer comparisons. The posted range is subject to change in the future. title: Product Certification Engineer, Fuel Cell Systems
descriptionHtml:
About EH Energy Engineering

EH Energy is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy-duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product delivers a significantly more compact fuel cell system with high power density and lower production costs. In response to the challenges of climate change and the global shift toward decentralized energy, EH Energy provides high-performance, cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

To support our rapid growth and bring our systems to global markets, we are seeking a Certification Engineer. In this critical role, you will take full ownership of our product compliance roadmap, bridging the gap between innovative engineering and strict global regulations. You will lead hazard and risk assessments, define certification strategies across international markets (EU, North America, marine), and interface directly with notified bodies and classification societies to ensure our fuel cell systems are safe, fully compliant, and market-ready.

This role requires a full-time, on-site presence at our office in Nyon, Switzerland. We are unable to offer remote or hybrid arrangements, so candidates should be based locally or prepared to relocate.

 

Key responsibilities

Certification strategy and project management

  • Identify applicable directives, regulations, harmonised standards and class rules early in the development cycle and translate them into design requirements (EU, North America, marine)

  • Select and manage notified bodies, NRTLs, classification societies and test laboratories, own budgets, schedules and contracts for certification work

  • Plan and witness type tests, factory acceptance tests (FAT) and site acceptance tests (SAT)

Safety engineering and risk analysis

  • Lead risk assessments to ISO 12100 and hazard studies (HAZID, HAZOP to IEC 61882)

  • Lead design and process FMEA (IEC 60812) for stacks, balance of plant, containers and fuel processing

  • Run explosion-protection assessments: hazardous area classification (IEC 60079-10-1), ventilation and gas detection concepts, and equipment selection

  • Specify and verify safety functions to ISO 13849 (PL) and IEC 61508, including safety requirement specifications and validation reports

Compliance and technical documentation

  • Compile and maintain technical construction files, CE Declarations of Conformity, type-approval dossiers and certification reports

  • Write and review user, installation, operation and maintenance manuals, safety instructions and labelling

  • Maintain the standards register and assess the impact of new or revised standards

  • Manage certification change control: assess design changes for impact on existing certificates

Collaboration and continuous improvement

  • Act as the internal authority on certification scope: ensure in-service conformity of series production with certified designs, and support procurement and supply chain on material and packaging compliance (e.g. RoHS, packaging regulations).

  • Support design reviews and supplier qualification, including component certificates (ATEX, PED, electrical)

Standards and regulatory scope

The role covers, but is not limited to, the frameworks below. Working knowledge of most is expected; deep expertise in several is required

  • IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1:2021, ISO 16110-1 and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230

     

Required qualifications

  • Master’s or bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, chemical, process or safety engineering, or equivalent

  • 5+ years in product certification, compliance or safety engineering for complex electromechanical or process equipment (energy, gas, process, machinery or marine)

  • Direct experience with hydrogen or fuel cell systems and the IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1 or ISO 16110

  • Proven track record of taking products through CE marking and third-party certification with notified bodies or NRTLs

  • Hands-on experience leading FMEA, HAZOP and risk assessments, and documenting them to auditor standard

  • Solid knowledge of ATEX / IECEx, hazardous area classification and explosion-protection concepts

  • Experience specifying and validating safety functions to ISO 13849 and/or IEC 61508

  • Excellent technical writing: clear, structured, audit-ready technical files and manuals

  • Fluent English, written and spoken

     

Preferred qualifications and personal profile

Nice to have

  • Marine type approval with a classification society (DNV, LR, BV, ABS) or IGF Code projects

  • Experience with fuel processing, reformers or fire equipment, and with pressure equipment under PED

  • Certified functional safety qualification or ATEX/IECEx competence certification

  • Familiarity with North American codes (NEC, NFPA) and UL/CSA certification

Personal profile

  • Rigorous and structured, with a strong safety mindset and an eye for detail

  • Pragmatic: finds compliant solutions that keep development moving

  • Confident communicator with engineers, auditors, authorities and customers

  • Self-driven in a fast-growing, scale-up environment; comfortable owning topics end to end

     

Start date: Immediately

descriptionHtml:
Ready to design products and services that make a difference?

Do you want to create products that make a meaningful impact? Are you ready to lead strategy and delivery on projects that reach large audiences?

If so, Opencast could be the place for you. We’re a growing tech consultancy that creates user-centred solutions with purpose for our clients in government, healthcare and purpose-driven businesses. As a Product Manager, you’ll lead product strategy and delivery, balancing user needs and business goals across sectors, to create services that are used by millions of UK citizens.

The role

You’ll work with technical teams and stakeholders to develop solutions that deliver our clients’ strategic goals. You'll work in agile teams alongside people in a range of roles spanning design, development, and research.

You’ll help deliver the vision, helping to decide the features that each product needs and manage backlogs to meet our client preferences. You'll deliver discovery and ideation workshops across diverse groups of stakeholders.

Ensure that work is carried out in accordance with Opencast's quality, environmental, and information security policies and procedures, as well as applicable customer policies, standards, and procedures while working on client.

Requirements

This role involves weekly on-site working. Applicants should be able to travel, as part of their daily commute, to client sites in one of the following locations: Newcastle, Leeds or Manchester.

We’re looking for people who value in-person collaboration, enjoy building strong relationships, and are passionate about delivering solutions that make a real difference for our clients.

Due to the nature of this role, you must either hold active Security Check (SC) clearance or be eligible and willing to undergo the clearance process.

SC clearance is granted in line with UK Government security vetting requirements. Typically, applicants must have UK citizenship and have lived continuously in the UK for at least the past five years, with no single absence exceeding 28 consecutive days. Nationality and immigration status may also be considered as part of the vetting process. We are unable to progress applications from candidates who do not meet these requirements.

If you are unsure whether you meet the eligibility criteria, we encourage you to review the guidance or discuss this with us before applying.

We are recruiting for multiple positions, with opportunities available immediately and in the coming months. If you are interested in joining Opencast, we encourage you to apply.

Essential experience

To succeed in this role, you will need to show a depth of experience working as a product manager, on complex projects across the product life cycle. You will need a good knowledge of software development and be familiar with agile processes and user-centred design.

In your CV and the interview, you should show how you have:
  • Recent government (public sector) experience and/or experience of delivering complex digital services that meet Government Digital Service (GDS) standards.
  • Developed and gained buy-in for product visions and minimum viable products
  • Used service design tools to map and articulate the wider ecosystems around products
  • Translated product roadmaps into backlogs to prioritise delivery
  • Balanced the needs of senior stakeholders to deliver successful outcomes
  • Excellent communication and relationship management skills
  • Contributed to constructive and trusting team environments

As well as product management skills, there are essential core skills you’ll need to be a great consultant.

In your interview, please show how you have:

  • Taken a methodical and considered approach to solving complex problems
  • Planned your own tasks, to achieve the objectives of your project
  • Positively challenged decisions or solutions you don’t agree with

With a significant proportion of our client base in the public sector, we are particularly interested in candidates with experience working in central or local government and/or the NHS.

Experience working to the GOV.UK Service Standards, including passing service standard assessments at different stages, is a key requirement. If you have this experience, please demonstrate this on your CV to discuss at interview.

Essential consulting skills

In addition to business analysis skills, there are essential core skills you’ll need to be an Opencast consultant. You’ll need to demonstrate how you:

  • Contribute to improving ways of working and driving continuous improvements within your teams.
  • Share knowledge and best practice with fellow product managers and other disciplines, including proactively engaging in client and Opencast communities of practice.
  • Positively challenge decisions or solutions you don’t agree with, striving for the best client outcomes.
  • Create lasting value in the projects you work on, ensuring a user-centric, sustainable approach.
  • Engage with Opencast in a meaningful way, supporting the growth of your practice and wider capability.
  • Support Opencast's growth plans, by providing case studies and updates into the relevant forums of your project work.

During the interview process, we’ll ask questions to explore your experience across these areas.

In the interview we’ll ask you questions that demonstrates this experience. We’ll also ask you questions based around these topics.

Salary

£50,000 - £59,000 per annum.

What we offer

A competitive package including a 7% employer pension contribution, share options, and a discretionary bonus. You’ll also benefit from 25 days’ holiday and access to 3 annual “life happens” days to support unexpected situations. We provide wellbeing support, ongoing professional development, volunteering opportunities, and the chance to be part of a genuinely supportive team.

Where you’ll work

This role requires regular on-site attendance at our HQ, hub offices, and client sites, as well as the ability to work from home. Applicants must be able to travel to offices and client sites across the UK as part of their normal working arrangements, as travel is essential for fulfilling the responsibilities of the role.

We include you

We welcome candidates from all identities, attributes, ways of thinking and backgrounds to thrive in a career at Opencast. Our aim is for the diversity of our people to be reflected in the solutions we deliver, to help create a fairer society for all.

Interview

Interviews will be conducted via Microsoft Teams. We’re happy to make adjustments to support your needs.

Visit our website or email

title: Product Manager (Web & App)
descriptionHtml:
Shape how tens of thousands of patients experience Wellis digitally, from first website visit to long-term treatment. Own the roadmap for our web platform and mobile app, and drive experiments that improve conversion, retention, and satisfaction.

Introduction

The digital patient journey at Wellis is growing rapidly and becoming more complex. To take it to the next level, we're looking for a Product Manager Web & App. You will own the product roadmap and prioritization across our web platform and mobile app-from first visit and prescription flow through onboarding, subscriptions, and long-term engagement. Working closely with engineering, UX/UI, data, and key stakeholders across medical operations, marketing, and customer care, you'll turn insights into shipped improvements and experiments that lift conversion, retention, and satisfaction. This is a hands-on role with real ownership for an experienced product builder who wants to make Wellis' digital experience the benchmark in healthcare.

About Wellis

Wellis is a fast-growing healthtech scale-up that is reinventing one of the most traditional sectors: healthcare. What started just three years ago has already grown into a company with tens of thousands of customers, and we are only at the beginning. By combining medical expertise with technology and data, we make healthcare smarter, more efficient, and more personal.

Our mission is to improve everyday lives by making care accessible, personal, and seamless. Through our platform, people can take control of their health journey with trusted medical support, smart digital tools, and tailored programs. We move fast, challenge conventions, and build solutions that truly make an impact, because we believe better healthcare should be within everyone's reach.

About the Role

As a Product Manager Web & App, you'll own the product direction for Wellis's web platform and mobile app across the full digital patient journey - from first visit through long-term treatment. You'll translate business goals, user needs, and medical requirements into a clear roadmap, and partner closely with design and engineering to ship improvements that drive conversion, retention, and satisfaction. With a strong eye for data and user insight, you'll identify friction points, run experiments with our CRO specialist, and align stakeholders across the business to keep the product vision sharp and execution moving fast.

You will start by owning the web platform and the mobile app together across the full digital patient journey. Both are first-class products. As the team grows, ownership may concentrate more on the app. We want someone who thrives owning both at the start and can adapt if focus deepens into mobile later.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the product roadmap and prioritization for Wellis's web platform and mobile app, translating business goals and user needs into clear features and improvements.

  • Define, scope, and deliver product initiatives across the full digital patient journey - from first visit to long-term treatment and subscription management.

  • Run product experiments together with our CRO specialist (A/B tests, feature releases) to improve conversion, retention, and user experience.

  • Work closely with UX/UI and engineering to ship high-quality features that support weight management treatments, subscriptions, and the broader wellness platform.

  • Analyze user behavior data, customer feedback (e.g., via Intercom), and medical team insights to identify friction points and opportunities for innovation.

  • Set clear product objectives and success metrics, and continuously track outcomes (including conversion, app/feature adoption, and NPS for the digital experience).

  • Align and manage stakeholders across medical operations, customer care, marketing, and leadership, while maintaining a clear product vision.

  • Communicate roadmap progress, trade-offs, and learnings clearly, and help the organization make data-informed product decisions.

About the Team

In this role, you'll work day-to-day with Engineering and UX/UI to define, prioritize, and ship improvements across our web platform and mobile app. You'll also partner closely with colleagues in marketing & growth, data & analytics, medical operations, and customer care to translate business goals and patient needs into a clear roadmap and to validate decisions through research and experimentation. As our digital domain is growing fast, you'll have a key role in shaping how we build product at Wellis and how teams collaborate across the full digital patient journey.


Who You Are

  • Extremely entrepreneurial and resourceful. You invent paths when playbooks do not exist, and you ship without waiting for perfect conditions.

  • Strong product instincts. You have a clear sense for what patients and the business need next, including when the data is incomplete.

  • This role is 100% AI- and agent-enabled. You are comfortable with an agentic product development process and with working with agents as part of how you build. You have clearly shown proficient use of agentic systems such as Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, Grok, or Cursor. Bring specific instances. Examples include shipping a feature end to end with agents, turning a backlog into agent-runnable specs, or cutting cycle time by pairing with coding agents. We will ask for those examples in the process.

  • Bachelor's or Master's level education.

  • 5+ years of experience as a Product Manager or Product Owner for web platforms and mobile apps.

  • Experienced in a start-up/scale-up environment, comfortable with speed, ambiguity, and pragmatism.

  • Strong at translating business goals and user needs into a clear roadmap, priorities, and well-defined product requirements.

  • Data-informed and outcome-driven; able to define and track product KPIs like conversion, adoption, retention, and NPS.

  • Comfortable running experiments (e.g., A/B tests, feature releases) and collaborating with a CRO specialist on hypotheses and success criteria.

  • Confident partnering daily with engineering and UX/UI to ship intuitive, high-quality experiences across the digital patient journey.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence without formal authority across medical, operations, marketing, and leadership.

  • Curious and customer-focused; skilled at turning feedback and insights into concrete product improvements.

  • Fluent in English;

  • Experience in healthcare, subscriptions, or marketplace/e-commerce environments is a plus.

What We Offer

  • The opportunity to help build a fast-growing healthtech scale-up from the inside.

  • A hands-on Product Manager role with real ownership of the web platform and mobile app roadmap.

  • Close collaboration with engineering, design, medical operations, marketing, customer care, data, and leadership.

  • The chance to make our web platform and mobile app the envy of everyone else - improving conversion, retention, and the end-to-end patient journey.

  • A culture of short lines, speed, pragmatism, and continuous improvement - where impact matters.

  • Hybrid working: partly from our new office in central Rotterdam, partly remote (We are flexible on that so dont hesitate to apply)

Hiring Process

  • Introductory chat with Georgios (Recruitment Lead) – an informal online call to get to know you and answer your questions.

  • Interview with the CTO – a deep-dive conversation about the role, your experience, and Wellis' ambitions.

  • Case & presentation – you'll prepare a case on site and present it to at least 2 stakeholders. This way, you get to know us better, and we get to know you.

  • Final conversation with the founders – a closing meeting where you'll hear more about the bigger Wellis story and feel whether this is the right place for you.

We keep the process compact and clear: you'll always know what to expect and truly get to know our team before making your decision.

title: Product Marketer
descriptionHtml:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

Summary

Dust is looking for a Product Marketer to shape how we bring a fast-moving, technical product to market and build the engine behind our product launches.

You will lead product launches and storytelling at Dust, turning a constant stream of product innovation into clear positioning, compelling narratives, and launches that help customers understand what’s new, why it matters, and what they can do with it.

This is a hands-on role. You will work closely with product and engineering to understand what we’re building, find the story within it, and bring that story to life across messaging, web, video, social, customer communications, and sales enablement. You’ll own the work from strategy through execution, bringing in designers, contractors, and other partners where they can add specialist expertise.

It’s a rare opportunity to help define the product narrative of a category-defining AI company while the product, the market, and the way people work with AI are all evolving quickly.

What you'll do

Own Dust’s product launch motion

  • Own product launches from initial narrative and positioning through asset creation, amplification strategy, and sales enablement

  • Build and run an always-on launch program that keeps pace with Dust’s rapid product development, supporting at least 5-7 releases each quarter

  • Partner closely with engineering team to understand what’s shipping, why it matters, and which initiatives require a broader market moment

  • Establish lightweight launch tiers and processes that bring consistency without slowing the team down

Turn product innovation into compelling stories

  • Develop positioning and messaging for new capabilities, translating technical innovation into clear, differentiated narratives that resonate with Dust’s buyers and users

  • Create launch assets across formats, including short-form videos, social campaigns, web copy, blogs, livestream events, customer communications, and sales collateral

  • Develop unique, scroll-stopping feature overview videos by owning storyboarding and screen capture end-to-end, while leveraging in-house creative and design support or external contractors as needed

  • Experiment with new formats and approaches to find the most effective ways to make Dust’s product understandable, memorable, and exciting

Become a trusted partner to product and engineering

  • Build strong relationships with engineers and user leads and become a partner they proactively bring into product launches

  • Develop enough technical fluency to ask the right questions, challenge assumptions, and uncover the most important customer and market story

  • Operate effectively in Dust’s highly autonomous product environment, where engineers often lead product initiatives directly

  • Bring customer, competitive, and market context into conversations about how we position and communicate the product

  • Partner with Dust’s founders and marketing leadership on major product narratives and moments

Connect product storytelling across the business

  • Equip Sales and Customer Success teams with the messaging, assets, and context they need to effectively pitch new capabilities to customers

  • Partner with Brand & Content to turn product innovation into broader editorial and content opportunities

  • Work with Growth and Field Marketing to extend launches across campaigns, events, and distribution channels

  • Ensure Dust’s product positioning and differentiation remain clear and consistent as the platform evolves

  • Create a reliable pipeline of high-quality product content that teams across Dust can use and distribute

What you’ll bring

  • 3–5+ years of dedicated product marketing experience, ideally with strong PMM foundations from an established B2B technology company and hands-on experience in a high-growth startup

  • A track record of personally owning technical B2B product or feature launches from positioning through execution

  • Exceptional product storytelling skills, with the ability to make complex technology clear, credible, and compelling

  • The range to create across formats, including positioning and messaging, web, written content, social, presentations, and video or demo storytelling

  • Strong technical curiosity and the ability to build credibility with engineers by asking thoughtful questions and quickly getting fluent in the product

  • Strong taste and an informed point of view on what great modern product marketing looks like

  • Comfort operating with ambiguity and figuring out the right approach rather than defaulting to an established playbook

  • A hands-on working style. You’re as comfortable writing the copy, developing the storyboard, or building the launch plan as you are setting the strategy

  • Deep fluency in and curiosity about AI. You’ll use Dust to run your own function and become deeply familiar with how our customers are putting AI to work

  • Based in Paris

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

  • Our product constitution, a story about our mission

  • Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human, Stanislas Polu, VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them.

  • Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI, Gabriel Hubert, Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe.

title: Product Owner - Acquitech
descriptionHtml:
Product Owner - Sales & Marketing, Acquisition Technology

Hybrid in London, UK

We're looking for a Product Owner to join the Acquitech team.

You'll own the roadmap for the team behind iwoca's acquisition data, technology and models.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don't wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that's as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star service ensure business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We've already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £5 billion in funding. Our team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they power.

The team

Acquitech builds and maintains the data infrastructure behind iwoca's direct acquisition channels. The team's aim is to get the right data to the right places – so ad platforms find businesses worth reaching, analysts trust the reports they build, and the sales team knows who to call first.

The team works across four areas:

  • Tracking and attribution. Recording every lead and sign-up accurately, and sending conversion data back to ad platforms so their algorithms improve over time.

  • Customer value prediction. Building models that estimate a potential customer's expected value, used to guide where marketing spends, who receives direct mail and which businesses a salesperson prioritises.

  • The data layer. Providing a clear, trusted foundation so analysts and channel managers can build reporting without second-guessing the numbers.

  • Team tooling and automation. Building tools and automated workflows, from automating sales task assignment to running LLM analysis on sales calls so the team can review performance at scale.

The team is small – three engineers, two data scientists and you – with the senior engineer sharing the day-to-day leadership. You'll report to a Senior Product Owner in an adjacent team.

The role

As Product Owner in Acquitech, you'll turn requests from marketing and sales into well-scoped work the team can deliver, and own the roadmap. You'll have real ownership of systems that directly shape acquisition spend, and the space to move quickly in a small, capable team. The work mixes delivery – compliance sign-offs, ad platform integrations and product changes – with discovery cycles where you prototype and test ideas quickly.

You'll become the go-to person for Acquitech systems and processes, and you'll use AI to multiply what a small team can deliver – from prototyping ideas to automating workflows for the team and its stakeholders.

  • Roadmap and priorities. You'll own priorities across Acquitech's work, writing clear requirements and seeing them through to release. You'll set direction with the Head of Direct Acquisition and the channel leads who depend on the team.

  • Tracking and ad platform integrations. You'll lead the team's work on conversion tracking, custom audiences and API migrations. You'll own the product change documentation that comes with them, working through Compliance, Data Privacy and Legal.

  • Discovery. You'll run discovery work to find new opportunities, using AI to prototype and test ideas quickly, and bring findings back to the wider business – for example through weekly learning sessions.

  • Ways of working. You'll run the team's rhythms – stand-ups, retros and monthly reviews – and set clear quarterly goals.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Product ownership. You've worked in a product role, managing several projects end to end – writing requirements, owning priorities and being accountable for results.

  • Data literacy. You use data to diagnose problems, size opportunities and evaluate whether a release delivered what you hoped.

title: Quadrants: Compiler Lead
descriptionHtml:
What Quadrants is

Quadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research.

The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton.

It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public.

The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast.

The role

You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap.

Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further.

It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows.

The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX.

Your mandate is to build the best open-source Python compiler for physics simulation out there. No limit on what that takes. If it means replacing the entire engine, your call. Either way, you keep Quadrants healthy and unblocking the company in the meantime.

What you’ll own

  • API & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. Idiomatic, natural to Python users, never a separate language bolted onto Python. Clean decorators, legible constraints, sharp errors, real escape hatches.

  • IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality.

  • Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform.

  • Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking.

  • Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. Propose API changes that cut duplication, improve readability, and reduce platform-specific special-casing. Less to maintain, more that simply works.

  • The project as a product. Benchmark real workloads, track performance over time, catch regressions early. Stay close to users (Genesis first), find friction and missing abstractions, drive adoption, set direction.

Who you are

You reason about whole systems and have taste for where complexity should live. You measure before you optimize, and you reach for memory traffic and launch overhead before FLOPs. You have opinions about API design. You write tests and benchmarks as you go, not afterward.

The ground that judgment stands on:

  • GPU. What optimal looks like and why: access patterns, registers, shared memory, barriers, atomics, threading. CPU intuition a plus.

  • Python & API taste. Idiomatic Python. A feel for what’s natural to Python users. APIs that free users rather than constrain them.

  • Compilers. The path from authoring to kernels (IR, lowering, optimization), weighed against maintainability.

And how you work: proactive and largely self-directed. You fetch context across the company instead of waiting for it. You’re comfortable talking to the engineers who use what you build, and at ease designing in the open for users you’ll never meet. Ready to grow into leading a small team (a couple of people, near term).

What great looks like

People adopt Quadrants from outside Genesis. Engineers write clearer code with less boilerplate. Kernels keep getting faster. Performance is tracked, not guessed. The architecture gets easier to extend, not harder.

What we’re uncompromising about

How you work is up to you. What matters is that your ownership grows over time: blind spots shrink, the parts you can vouch for expand, technical debt goes down, the core stays sound.

That takes treating understanding as real work, not overhead. You read and challenge the codebase instead of just stacking features on it. You take nothing you did not write for granted. You watch the competition and what’s coming next, and you bring it in and ship it.

Use AI agents if they help. They are productivity tools, not code owners. You are.

title: Quantitative Researcher, Marketplace
descriptionHtml:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

Relay makes millions of dynamic, interconnected decisions across its network every day, and each one shapes the experience of the thousands of couriers who work with us. Knowing what any one of those decisions actually did is hard: couriers interfere with each other, effects vary from person to person, and the outcomes that matter compound over time.

Science at Relay is the brain of the operation: machine learning, operational research, recommender systems, causal inference, location intelligence and experimentation, working together to decide how every parcel gets delivered. You'll lead causal inference at Relay from the start.

Causal Inference Highlights

  • A live, two-sided marketplace to experiment in, with every decision logged across millions of parcels.

  • Interference between couriers, heterogeneous effects and long-term outcomes are the norm here, not the exception.

  • Four marketplaces, each with its own app and its own economics.

  • Your insights and models feed straight into Relay's network-wide optimisation.

The Opportunity

As a Quantitative Researcher at Relay, you'll:

  • Set the standard for causal inference at Relay.

  • Measure how our decisions affect each courier, today and over time.

  • Shape how Relay experiments across a live, two-sided marketplace.

  • Adapt advanced techniques across causal inference, statistics and machine learning to Relay's problems, and see them through to production.

  • Partner with Operational Research to embed your insights and models into Relay's network-wide optimisation, and help build our research culture and voice in the tech community.

We're looking for candidates who…

  • Bring deep expertise in causal inference, experimentation and machine learning, whether from a PhD, publications, or years at the frontier in industry.

  • Come from statistics, an experimental science such as biology or psychology, or quantitative research.

  • Have applied advanced techniques to real marketplaces or products, and owned the outcome.

  • Think in mechanisms, and let evidence guide decisions.

  • Are energised by open, interconnected problems, and know how to find the signal.

  • Collaborate generously, and explain complex ideas simply.

Don't tick every box? If this problem excites you, we'd still love to hear from you.

Who Thrives at Relay?

  • Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.

  • Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

  • 1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

  • All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.

  • People-Powered Greatness: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.

  • Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.

    If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.

Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.

  • Query performance and data access. Creating and optimising query performance and data access patterns.

  • Building backend systems that stand up to production load. Reliability, throughput, and durability are part of the job, not someone else's.

  • Scalable APIs and services. Designing and implementing API endpoints and services that handle real customer traffic.

  • Security as a default. Applying security best practices in everything you ship.

  • Monitoring, logging, and debugging. Implementing the observability tooling that lets us spot problems and fix them fast.

  • Architecture and technical roadmap. Contributing to architectural decisions and shaping where the platform goes next.

We build in public, so you can see some of the things you might work on here.

Working at a Commercial Open Source Software company is more than just coding:

  • We have an active community on Discord and GitHub. Everyone on the team helps customers, reviews PRs, and creates issues.

  • Having great documentation is essential. Everyone writes docs.

  • We're a product-led growth company, so everyone is expected to get involved in creating content like code examples, blog articles, videos, and tweets.

Requirements

You really need to have:

  • Expertise in Node.js and TypeScript. We use Remix.

  • Expertise with Postgres and Redis. You've designed schemas, tuned queries, and run these in production.

  • Cloud infrastructure experience. AWS, GCP, or Azure.

  • Comfortable being on call. Reliability is a shared responsibility for the engineering team.

  • Open to in-person events throughout the year. If you're remote, we'll arrange these so the team gets real time together.

You'll be an amazing fit if you have:

  • A proven track record of contributing to open source projects.

  • Previously been a venture-backed startup founder.

  • Experience with React, or better still, Remix.

  • Worked on a high throughput system.

  • Designed SDKs for developers.

  • Experience with self-managed Kubernetes.

  • Familiarity with Linux.

  • OTel or "o11y" experience.

  • Worked at a developer tools company.

  • Experience with Go.

About the team

  • We are a small team with a flat hierarchy.

  • We encourage continuous learning and personal development.

  • Everyone operates autonomously; we trust you to get the job done, but to also quickly raise your hand if you need help.

  • We care about our customers and the open-source community.

  • Being a start-up, the work is challenging and fast-paced, but we also understand the importance of taking time off to recharge.

Benefits

  • Generous, transparent compensation and equity - We hire the best talent and pay to reflect that. We also offer equity as a way to ensure everyone is invested in the success of the company.

  • Async working - Need a heads-down day or meeting-free days to stay productive? No problem!

  • Home office - We will help provide equipment for a comfortable setup so you're as productive at home as you are in the office.

  • Generous vacation - We believe it's important to take time off. We encourage you to take your 25 days vacation excluding national holidays, plus sick leave and generous parental leave.

  • Training budget - An annual budget to contribute towards learning such as purchasing books, an Audible subscription or online courses.

  • Pension and 401k contributions - Enroll in our company pension scheme or we'll contribute directly to your private pension.

Our values

  • We are proud to be open source - We believe in the open source community and building a great free-to-use product. We encourage community contributions and are public about what we are building.

  • We ship uncomfortably fast - As a startup, moving fast is key. We are pragmatic about what we build, when we build it, and value iterative development above all.

  • Working autonomously - We don't tell you what to do. We decide as a team what will have the biggest impact for our customers and prioritise what we work on from that.

Interview process

  1. Application. We'll review your application, CV, and any code samples or open source contributions you share.

  2. Screening call. A chat about your background, the systems you've built, and what you're looking for next.

  3. Hiring manager call. A deeper technical conversation about your work and how you'd approach the role.

  4. Paid task day. You'll spend a paid day working on a real engineering problem with us, then walk us through your thinking with the team.

  5. Final interview. A call with a couple of members of the wider team to answer any remaining questions and align on culture fit.

  6. References & offer. If everyone is happy, we'll make you an offer to join us.

If this sounds like your dream job, we can't wait to hear from you. If you're not sure that you exactly fit these requirements, get in touch anyway!

title: Senior Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Filiz est une startup SaaS de 30 personnes qui digitalise aujourd'hui les contrats d'apprentissage en France et construit son deuxième produit : un ERP nouvelle génération pour transformer la façon dont les établissements d'enseignement supérieur opèrent au quotidien.

Depuis 2025, Filiz est accompagnée par Hexa, le startup studio français derrière des succès de licornes comme Spendesk, Aircall et Front.

Nous attaquons un marché immense, encore largement à réinventer. Le premier produit est en production, les clients sont là. Maintenant, nous entrons dans une nouvelle phase : construire un produit ambitieux, sortir de France et bâtir la référence européenne des outils pour l'enseignement supérieur.

Nous cherchons un(e) Senior Software Engineer capable de prendre l'ownership d'un produit, d'une architecture et d'un domaine technique, tout en restant profondément hands-on. Le poste n'a pas de management hiérarchique : ton impact passe par le code, les choix d'architecture et la montée en compétence de l'équipe.

Intégré au sein d’une équipe, tu travailleras principalement sur l'ERP, encore en construction : tu participeras à le concevoir et à l'amener jusqu'à la production. Le produit historique reste en production et l'équipe continue de le faire vivre.

Ce que tu vas faire chez nous

  • Build & Run de A à Z : tu conçois et fais évoluer des features end-to-end : design, développement, releases et suivi en production.

  • Hands-on & design : tu codes, refactores et améliores l'existant. Tu participes à l'architecture avec le CTO et poses les bases d'un système capable de scaler.

  • PR review & excellence technique : tu élèves le niveau de l'équipe en challengeant le code, la modélisation, les cas limites et la maintenabilité.

  • Intégrations robustes : tu construis des APIs et des systèmes résilients adaptés à des contraintes métier fortes.

  • Fiabilité & observabilité : tu conçois des systèmes capables de détecter et prévenir les problèmes avant qu'ils n'atteignent les utilisateurs.

  • Leadership technique : tu accompagnes les développeurs de l'équipe, partages tes pratiques et fais grandir les personnes autour de toi.

Ce qui t'attend techniquement

  • Stack: TypeScript, Next.js, NestJS, MongoDB, Redis, AWS, monorepo Turborepo

  • Observabilité : Sentry, BetterStack, OpenTelemetry

  • Façon de travailler : Kanban, sans sprint. On livre en petits incréments et on deploy plusieurs fois par jour

Profil recherché

  • 6+ ans d'expérience avec une expérience prouvée sur des produits en production utilisés par de vrais utilisateurs.

title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
YOUR MISSION

 

A software engineer today uses Claude Code or Cursor. A mechanical engineer designing the next jet engine still searches Excel sheets and asks whoever has been around longest.

 

We are building the AI co-engineer for physical products: one that works natively in 3D and learns from real engineering decisions. We are in production with major European manufacturers, with real revenue and customers who tell us when we are slow.

 

The problems are open ones. Getting an agent to reason usefully about geometry, making 3D search work on real customer part libraries, and figuring out what the interface even looks like when an engineer asks why a bracket failed. There is research to borrow from and very little product to copy.

 

Senior or staff level depending on experience.

 

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 

You will own large problems end to end, across the stack. We cannot say exactly what that looks like in month three, but here is what the last two years have actually involved.

 

  • A multi-agent orchestration SDK, built from scratch. Nothing off the shelf handled what we needed: long-horizon execution that runs for hours and survives restarts.

  • CAD conversion as a real pipeline. It used to be manual and brittle. Turning it into production infrastructure meant writing a Python wrapper around a C++ SDK and making it reliable enough to sit under everything else.

  • Migrating the application off Electron and Webpack onto SSR React with Vite. That architecture is what the whole product now sits on.

 

What is coming:

 

  • 3D-to-3D search across real customer part libraries, not benchmark datasets

  • Constraint solvers and optimization, and getting an agent to use one sensibly

  • Agents that hold a useful model of a physical object, which is still an open problem

  • Hybrid cloud deployments for manufacturers who cannot send their data anywhere

 

We work in Python and TypeScript, with multi-agent orchestration and AI integrations across several providers.

 

WHAT WE CARE ABOUT

 

  • You have shipped production systems across frontend and backend, and can point at them

  • Your CV reads as a set of problems, not a stack

  • You use AI heavily to go faster, but you built things the hard way first

  • You are fine when the problem is not yet defined

  • You deliver end to end, and you are still there when it needs maintaining

 

Bonus: CAD, computational geometry, constraint solving or optimization, 3D, LLM agents, industrial software. None required.
